newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF panel says cut in futures trading costs needed.
newsitem.headline: MOF panel says cut in futures trading costs needed.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance's (MOF) Financial System Research Council (FSRC) has concluded that transaction costs need to be cut in order to make trading in financial futures more active, a MOF official said.

During an FSRC meeting on Thursday, Yasuhiko Kato, senior managing director of Tokyo International Financial Futures Exchange (TIFFE), said he would like to see the abolition of an exchange tax so as to reduce the cost of trading in the Tokyo market, the official said.
Members of TIFFE who trade in yen financial futures are charged an exchange tax equivalent to 0.01 percent of the transaction amount.

The cost of trading a short-term yen futures contract is about twice that in overseas markets such as the Singapore International Monetary Exchange and the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange because those who trade on TIFFE are charged the exchange tax in addition to a set membership fee.
When asked about MOF's position on the exchange tax, the official said financial transactions would probably take place more smoothly if an exchange tax was not levied.
